long.title: A Year Without a Car
long.text:
When my old car finally broke down last January, the mechanic told me that repairing it would cost more than the car was worth. I was annoyed at first, because I had driven to work every day for ten years. But my sister suggested an experiment: why not try living without a car for a whole year? I laughed at the idea, but I agreed to try it for one month.
The first week was difficult. My office is eight kilometres from my flat, and I had to work out which buses to take. On the second day I got on the wrong one and arrived forty minutes late. My boss was not pleased. However, by the end of the week I had found a route that took only ten minutes longer than driving, and I could read on the bus instead of sitting in traffic.
After a month, I noticed some surprising changes. I was walking about six thousand more steps a day, and I slept better than I had for years. I was also saving money. Without paying for petrol, parking and insurance, I had almost two hundred dollars more each month. So I decided to continue the experiment.
Of course, there were problems. Shopping became more complicated, and I had to plan carefully before I went to the supermarket. Visiting my parents, who live in a village with only two buses a day, was the hardest part. A couple of times I had to borrow my sister's car, which she reminded me about often.
Now the year is over, and people keep asking me whether I will buy a new car. I'm still not sure. I miss the freedom of being able to go anywhere at any time, especially at weekends. But I don't miss the traffic or the cost. For now, I've bought a second-hand bicycle, and I've joined a car-sharing club for the occasional long journey. Perhaps that is the right balance for me.

qs.q: Why did the writer stop using the old car?
qs.a: It would cost too much to repair.
w: The writer's sister wanted to buy it.
The writer wanted to get more exercise.
qs.why: “repairing it would cost more than the car was worth.”

qs.q: What happened during the first week?
qs.a: The writer arrived late for work once.
w: The writer decided to stop the experiment.
The writer found a route faster than driving.
The writer's boss offered a lift to work.
qs.why: “On the second day I got on the wrong one and arrived forty minutes late.” Đường mới chậm hơn lái xe 10 phút, không nhanh hơn.
“I had almost two hundred dollars more each month.” Xe đạp mua cuối năm.

qs.q: What was the most difficult part of the year?
w: getting to the office on time
finding a bus to the supermarket
qs.why: “Visiting my parents, who live in a village… was the hardest part.”

qs.q: How does the writer feel at the end of the year?
qs.a: The writer has found a compromise that works for now.
w: The writer will definitely buy a new car soon.
The writer never wants to drive again.
The writer thinks everyone should give up their car.
qs.why: “For now, I've bought a second-hand bicycle… Perhaps that is the right balance for me.”

long.title: Learning on the Job
long.text:
Most cafés hire staff who already know how to make coffee and serve customers. The Green Door café in Hue does the opposite. Every one of its waiters, cooks and baristas is a young person who has never had a job before. The café is part of a training programme for teenagers who left school early, and after six months there, most of them go on to find work in hotels and restaurants.
The idea came from Minh Chau, a former hotel manager. 'When I was interviewing people for jobs, I met so many young people who were clever and hard-working but had no experience,' she explains. 'Nobody wanted to give them a chance, so they couldn't get experience. I wanted to break that circle.'
Trainees spend their mornings in a classroom above the café, where they study English, food safety and customer service. In the afternoons they work downstairs with real customers. Mistakes happen, of course. 'On my first day I dropped a whole tray of drinks,' laughs Nam, who is seventeen. 'I wanted to run away. But the customers were really kind, and my trainer showed me how to carry the tray properly.'
Customers seem happy to be part of the project. Many of them are tourists who have read about the café online, but there are also local office workers who come in every day. A small notice on each table explains the programme and asks customers to be patient. 'The coffee is excellent and the service is friendly,' says one regular customer. 'If it's a bit slow sometimes, I don't mind at all.'
The café does not make much profit, and it depends on donations to pay for the classes. Minh Chau admits that money is a constant worry. But she has no plans to give up. Last year, forty-two trainees finished the programme, and thirty-eight of them are now in full-time jobs. 'That number,' she says, 'is the only profit I really care about.'

qs.q: What is unusual about the Green Door café?
qs.a: None of its staff had worked before.
w: It only employs experienced hotel workers.
It is only open to tourists.
It trains people to open their own cafés.
qs.why: “a young person who has never had a job before.”

qs.q: Why did Minh Chau start the programme?
qs.a: She saw that young people could not get their first job.
w: She was unhappy working as a hotel manager.
She needed more staff for her hotel.
She wanted to teach English to tourists.
qs.why: “Nobody wanted to give them a chance, so they couldn't get experience.”

qs.a: Trainees get support when they make mistakes.
w: Trainees often leave after their first day.
The work is too difficult for most teenagers.
Trainees are not allowed to serve drinks.
qs.why: “the customers were really kind, and my trainer showed me how to carry the tray properly.”

qs.q: What do the customers think of the café?
qs.a: They accept that the service is sometimes slow.
w: They come mainly because the coffee is cheap.
They would prefer more experienced staff.
They find the notice on the tables annoying.
qs.why: “If it's a bit slow sometimes, I don't mind at all.”

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
qs.a: to describe a project that helps young people find work
w: to advertise a new café to tourists
to explain how to become a hotel manager
to complain about the lack of jobs for teenagers
qs.why: Cả bài nói về chương trình giúp người trẻ có việc (38/42 người có việc).

At first I couldn't run more than two kilometres without {3} a break, but the coach gave me a training plan and I soon {4} the difference. Last month I {5} part in my first ten-kilometre race. gaps.why: join a club = vào câu lạc bộ; belong cần “to”.
make sb feel… = làm ai cảm thấy; cause cần “to feel”.

mc.title: A Message from the Library
mc.text: Dear members, we are pleased to {1} you that the city library will reopen on 3rd June after six months of building work. The new library has a larger children's section and a quiet room where you can study {2} being disturbed. We have also {3} the number of computers from ten to thirty. mc.title: The Story of Pho
mc.text: Pho is now famous all over the world, but it has a fairly short {1}. Most historians {2} with the idea that it first appeared in northern Vietnam in the early twentieth century. At that time, it was sold by street sellers who {3} their kitchens on their shoulders. After 1954, many people moved south and {4} the dish with them. carry on their shoulders = gánh trên vai.
take sth with them = mang theo.
a new style was born = ra đời.
depend on = phụ thuộc vào.

open.title: My Favourite Place
open.text: There is a small lake {1} the edge of my town where I often go at weekends. It is not famous, and there {2} never many people there, which is why I love it. I usually take a book and sit under a tree for hours. Last summer I saw a family of ducks {3} the first time. I have been going there {4} I was a child, and it has hardly changed. I hope it stays {5} same for many years, because it is the place {6} I feel most relaxed.

gaps.why: on / at the edge of = ở rìa.
there are + số nhiều (many people).
for the first time = lần đầu.
since + mốc thời gian (I was a child).
stay the same = giữ nguyên.
the place where = nơi mà.

open.title: An Email to a Friend
open.text: Hi Lan, thanks {1} your message. I'm sorry I didn't reply sooner, but I've been really busy {2} my exams. They finally finished yesterday, so now I can relax! Are you free {3} Saturday? There's a new film at the cinema that I'd love to see. If you don't like films, we {4} go to the beach instead. Let me know {5} you prefer. I'm really looking forward {6} seeing you. Love, Mai

gaps.why: thanks for = cảm ơn vì.
busy with sth = bận việc gì.
on Saturday / this Saturday / next Saturday.
động từ khuyết thiếu để gợi ý: we could go.
which / what you prefer = bạn thích cái nào.
look forward to + V-ing.

open.title: Why We Yawn
open.text: Everyone yawns, but scientists still are not completely sure why we {1} it. One popular idea is that yawning helps to cool the brain. When our brains get too warm, we may yawn {2} order to take in cooler air. Another interesting fact is that yawning is 'catching'. If you see someone yawn, you are much more likely {3} yawn yourself. Some studies suggest that this happens more often between friends {4} between strangers. Even reading {5} yawning can make people yawn. Are you yawning now? If so, you are not the only {6}!

gaps.why: do it = làm việc đó (thay cho yawn).
in order to = để.
be likely to + V.
more often … than = thường hơn so với.
read about sth = đọc về.
the only one = người duy nhất.

kwt.s1: I started learning English three years ago.
kwt.why: Hiện tại hoàn thành (tiếp diễn) + for + khoảng thời gian.

kwt.s1: It's not necessary to bring food.
The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
kwt.s2: It was ____ that I fell asleep.
kwt.why: so + tính từ = such + a + tính từ + danh từ.

kwt.s1: My brother is taller than me.
'I'll call you tomorrow,' Tom said to me.
kwt.s2: Tom said ____ me the next day.

kwt.s1: Somebody stole my bike last night.
kwt.why: Bị động quá khứ: was + V3.

kwt.s1: Shall we go swimming this afternoon?
I haven't been to the cinema for a long time.
kwt.s2: It's ____ I went to the cinema.
